💡 Quick summary

The RTS piece argues that digital maps have become geopolitical interfaces where platform choices increasingly shape territorial narratives once controlled by states.

📌 Key takeaways

  • RTS frames cartography as a political technology rather than a neutral mirror of geography.
  • The article uses Crimea to illustrate the stakes.
  • The second half broadens the discussion beyond digital platforms to world maps and projections.
  • A useful contribution of the article is that it connects local product decisions in digital maps with older cartographic debates about worldview, power, and representation.
